stem.en: Which statement about contact inhibition is correct?

text.en: Division in many animal cells usually stops when cells touch.

feedback.en: Yes. Cancer cells lose this control.

text.en: It makes cells divide faster when they touch their neighbours.

feedback.en: It stops division. It does not speed it up.

text.en: It is seen mostly in plant cells, because of their rigid walls.

feedback.en: Plant cells do not show contact inhibition.

text.en: It is the process in which gametes join during fertilisation.

feedback.en: This describes fertilisation only, not contact inhibition.

explanation.en: In many animal cells, division usually stops when cells come in contact with neighbouring cells.

hints.en: What does the word inhibition suggest?
